experiment: Amide HDX-MS of full-length CheA, 3 min uptake relative to fully exchanged control; P2 domain fraction with rapid uptake (>70% at 3 min); Waters SYNAPT G2Si
ligand_or_partner: none (free CheA in solution, 3 µM, about 75% dimeric)
construct_or_mutation: full-length E. coli CheA, TEV-cleavable His-tagged (P2 defined as residues 161 to 223)
other_conditions: Table 1 P2 rapid-uptake fraction 22% (kinase-off, free CheA); rapid defined as >70% uptake at 3 min; reported fractions are a lower limit since undetected peptides not counted; related structures: 6S1K, 2LP4
dynamics_type: domain stability by amide H/D exchange; P2 stable domain connected by disordered linkers
author_claim: P1, P2 and P3 are relatively stable domains in free CheA, in contrast to the unstable P4 and P5 domains.
anchor: Table 1  illustrates that P1, P2, and P3 are relatively stable domains for 3 μM CheA in solution, with 20 to 30% rapid uptake.
locator: Results, 'CheA in Solution Has Unstable Catalytic and Regulatory Domains'; Table 1; conditions: Methods, HDX-MS
caveat_note: Entry is a 69-residue P2 (CheY-binding) fragment, whereas this is full-length CheA, so the P2 behavior is in the multidomain context. Residues are not listed with one-letter types, so no residue mapping to the entry sequence was made. Low H/D exchange of a domain does not by itself identify specific motions.

experiment: Amide HDX-MS of CheA in vesicle-assembled complexes with CF4E and CheW; P2 domain fraction with rapid uptake at 3 min
ligand_or_partner: CF4E (unmethylated Asp receptor cytoplasmic fragment) and CheW on Ni2+-chelating lipid vesicles; 3 µM CheA, 18 µM CheW, 30 µM CF, 860 µM lipid
construct_or_mutation: full-length E. coli CheA, TEV-cleavable His-tagged (P2 defined as residues 161 to 223); His-tagged CF4E
other_conditions: Table 1 P2 rapid-uptake fraction 38% (partially kinase-off, CheA in CF4E complexes); about half the kinase activity of CF4Q complexes; 80 to 90% of CheA bound; related structures: 6S1K, 2LP4
dynamics_type: domain stability by amide H/D exchange in signaling complex
author_claim: CheA in CF4E complexes shows little change in overall uptake relative to solution (P3 destabilized), with P4 not stabilized and kinase activity low.
locator: Table 1 (columns: kinase-off 3 µM CheA, CF4E complexes, CF4Q complexes); conditions: Methods, HDX-MS
caveat_note: The rise in P2 rapid-uptake fraction from 22% to 38% in CF4E complexes is not interpreted by the authors, who focus on P3 destabilization. It is not clear whether it reflects a real P2 change or peptide coverage and thresholding. The authors note CF4E complexes are not a perfect kinase-off mimic. Residue types for P2 are not given, so no entry mapping was made.

experiment: Amide HDX-MS of CheA in vesicle-assembled complexes with CF4Q and CheW; P2 domain fraction with rapid uptake at 3 min
ligand_or_partner: CF4Q (methylation mimic, Asp receptor cytoplasmic fragment) and CheW on Ni2+-chelating lipid vesicles; 3 µM CheA, 18 µM CheW, 30 µM CF, 860 µM lipid
construct_or_mutation: full-length E. coli CheA, TEV-cleavable His-tagged (P2 defined as residues 161 to 223); His-tagged CF4Q
other_conditions: Table 1 P2 rapid-uptake fraction 22% (kinase-on, CheA in CF4Q complexes); specific activity 23 s-1; 80 to 90% of CheA bound; related structures: 6S1K, 2LP4
dynamics_type: domain stability by amide H/D exchange in kinase-on complex
author_claim: In kinase-on complexes P1 and P2 remain stable and mobile, while P3, P4 and P5 are stabilized; no significant change in initial uptake in P2.
anchor: Outside of the kinase core domains, there is no significant change in the initial uptake in P1, P2, and the linkers that connect them to the kinase core
locator: Results, 'Kinase Core Domains Are Stabilized in Kinase-On Complexes'; Table 1; conditions: Methods, HDX-MS
caveat_note: The unchanged P2 initial uptake only says there is no detectable change in 3-min H/D exchange protection. It does not exclude P2 motion on other timescales, and the authors say P1 and P2 stay mobile. Residue types for P2 are not given, so no entry mapping was made.

experiment: Amide HDX-MS difference uptake of CheA in CF4Q complexes with AMPPCP versus solution; P2 domain
ligand_or_partner: AMPPCP (10 mM, about 10X Ki of 877 µM) with CF4Q and CheW on vesicles
construct_or_mutation: full-length E. coli CheA, TEV-cleavable His-tagged; His-tagged CF4Q
other_conditions: about 90% of CheA in complexes expected to have AMPPCP bound; related structures: 6S1K, 2LP4, 1i58 (T. maritima P4 with AMPPCP, used for positioning AMPPCP)
dynamics_type: nucleotide-coupled stabilization; P1-P4 interaction reducing P2 solvent exposure
author_claim: AMPPCP binding causes widespread reduced uptake in P2, perhaps because P1 interactions with P4 reduce P2 solvent exposure.
anchor: In addition to the reduced uptake on both the dimerization and P4-binding surfaces of P1, we also observed widespread reduced uptake in P2 in the AMPPCP-bound state.
locator: Results, 'AMPPCP Binding Induces Further Stabilization That Promotes Transient Interactions of P1 with P4'; Fig. 3C; conditions: Methods, HDX-MS
caveat_note: The authors only speculate about the cause ('Perhaps interactions of P1 with P4 also reduce the solvent exposure of P2'). The reduced uptake could reflect stabilization, reduced exposure, or both. No residue-level P2 list with one-letter types is given, so no entry mapping was made.
